title: ANDS Studio — Validation, sequences & export
walkthrough:
Across the top of every page sits a persistent yellow banner: "Demo / evaluation environment — nothing here is transmitted to Health Canada and no email is sent. Use it to explore the full workflow safely."

In the dossier workspace, a card headed "Draft completeness check" summarizes the structural check of the dossier. In the card's top-right corner sits a status badge: "● NO STRUCTURAL ISSUES" when there are no errors, or a count such as "● 3 issue(s)" when there are. Below it, each finding appears on its own line: a small monospaced rule ID first (for example a value like CA-E-1001; if a finding has no ID, the fallback code "CA-E" is shown, or "CA-W" for warnings), then a small uppercase severity chip reading "error" (or "warning"), then — when the finding is tied to a specific document — the leaf name shown as a small monospaced code prefix followed by a colon, and finally the finding's message. Only the first five errors are listed; if there are more, a small button reads "Show all 12 findings" (with the real count), and after clicking it the same button reads "Show fewer". PDF/A-1b advisories are grouped separately: each appears as a muted, secondary row with an "advisory" chip, a line like "PDF/A-1b advisory (…) — 9 leaves · advisory only, does not block", and a "Review 9 items" expander (which toggles to "Hide itemized list") revealing one row per affected leaf. Other (non-PDF/A) warnings follow in the same row format as errors, capped at three; when more exist, a button reads "+4 more warning(s)" (with the real count) and toggles to "Show fewer warnings". If there are no errors and no warnings at all, a line reads: "No presence/format issues found. This does not confirm scientific adequacy or full eCTD validity — run eValidator before transmission."

A collapsed expander labeled "Technical check & report" (summary: "Run PDF header / encryption / PDF/A-1b structural sub-check · export CSV/JSON") holds the deeper check and the report exports. Opening it reveals a button labeled "Run technical check (PDF header / encryption / PDF/A-1b)". Clicking it disables the button and changes its label to "Checking…" while a deeper validation runs on the server; when it returns, the card's badge, error list, and warning list are replaced by the full result. Alongside it are "Download report (CSV)", "Download report (JSON)", and "Download report (PDF)" buttons. A fine-print line inside the expander reads: "Findings carry structural-rule ids (CA-E-…/CA-W-…) covering leaf integrity, lifecycle legality, naming, sequence numbering, XML backbone and the document payload: PDF header, encryption, and PDF/A-1b structural markers (XMP pdfaid packet, OutputIntent, PDF-1.4 base version, and prohibited active content). This is a presence/format completeness check — not a Health Canada review, not full eCTD technical validation, and not full ISO 19005-1 (PDF/A-1) conformance validation. Where a checksum is shown it is document control (md5), not validation."

To understand a rule ID, the user can open the Help page. Its top bar shows "ANDS Studio · regulatory reference" with navigation chips: "Journey", "Dossiers", "Portfolio", "Registry", "Correspondence", and "Help". The page heading is "Regulatory reference", introduced by: "The primary Health Canada sources behind everything this app checks and generates. Every in-app review finding links to one of these; this page collects them so you can read the rule, not just trust the tool. All links go to canada.ca / laws-lois.justice.gc.ca." Link cards, each opening in a new tab and marked with "↗", are grouped under three headings — "Filing an ANDS — the core references", "Generic-specific", and "Transmitting & after approval" — with one-line notes; the CESG card's note states a limit plainly: "This app prepares and simulates; the gateway account is yours."

Further down is the section "How validation works here". A card opens with "Every finding carries a rule ID you can cite in review meetings:" followed by bullets: "CA-E-1xxx — leaf inventory integrity: every live document needs an href and a well-formed MD5 checksum; duplicate leaf IDs are errors."; "CA-E-2xxx — lifecycle legality: replace/append/delete operations must reference a real prior leaf; new leaves can't claim one."; "CA-E-3xxx — file/folder naming hygiene (lowercase, no spaces, module folder placement)."; "CA-E-4xxx — sequence numbering."; "XML backbone (index + CA regional) and PDF conformance run in the full technical check on the stored bytes."; and "CA-REP-0001 — filing is blocked while a dossier still uses a placeholder ID instead of the REP-issued one." The card closes: "On top of the technical layer, each authorable form has a content review against Health Canada's required elements — every finding cites its canada.ca source and proposes the edit." Beneath it, a second card is titled in bold "The complete rule catalogue (42 rules, live from the engine)" — the count is fetched from the validation engine, so the number reflects whatever the API returns; while fetching, the card shows "Loading…". The rules are grouped into collapsible rows per family, each summarized like "leaf — 8 rules"; expanding one lists each rule as its ID, "(warning)" where the severity is warning, a dash, and its description.

Back in the workspace sidebar, a card labeled "Sequences" lists the dossier's eCTD sequences, with "working: 0001" (the active sequence number) at top right. Each row shows the four-digit sequence number in bold, a purpose chip reading "Response", "Supplement", "Annual notification", or "Initial" (hovering it reveals the sequence's note, if any), and a leaf count like "3 leaf(s)". The active sequence carries a "● ACTIVE" badge; every other row has a "Make active" button. Each row also has an "Export" chip whose tooltip reads "Download the eCTD package for sequence 0001" (its label changes to "Exporting…" while running). Clicking Export runs validation on the server. If validation passes, the package download starts. If it fails, the export is blocked and an in-panel notice appears in place of a download, headed "Export blocked — sequence 0001", with an explanation such as "The completeness check did not pass." (or, if the validator could not run at all, "Validation could not run, so export is blocked." — a validator that cannot be reached blocks the export, it does not proceed without the check). If the ruleset criteria are known, a muted line reads "Checked against <name> v<version>. This is a structural/format check — not a Health Canada review." The notice then lists up to eight blocking findings (each with its rule ID or rule, the leaf, and the message), and "+N more" if there are more than eight. To export in spite of the block, the user must type a reason under the label "To export anyway, type a reason (recorded to the audit trail):" into an input with placeholder "e.g. internal QA review only — not for transmission"; the "Export anyway (override)" button stays disabled until a reason is entered (and shows "Exporting…" while saving), and a "Cancel" button dismisses the notice. A "New sequence" button (disabled until the list loads) expands into a form headed "New sequence 0002" (the next number), a "Sequence purpose" dropdown defaulting to Response, a note field with placeholder "Note (e.g. screening deficiency SDN-1)", and two buttons: "Create & make active" (showing "Creating…" while saving) and "Cancel".
